newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvador trade deficit falls 25 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Salvador trade deficit falls 25 pct in first half.

text.p: El Salvador's trade deficit tumbled 25 percent to $549.8 million in the first half of 1997 from $733.4 million in the first six months of 1996, the Central Reserve Bank said Tuesday.
Exports grew 42 percent to $1.263 billion, while imports grew 11.7 percent to $1.813 billion, the central bank said.
The trade deficit stood at $436.5 million after the first five months of the year.
The central bank noted strong growth in manufacturing exports, up 41.2 percent to $495.8 million in the first half from $351.1 million a year earlier.
Traditional exports reached $407.9 million: coffee accounted for $344.6 million, followed by sugar at $49 million and shrimp at $14.3 million.
Traditional exports were up 71.1 percent from $237.5 million in the first half of 1996.
Non-traditional exports reached $359.3 million in the 1997 first half, up 19.4 percent from $300.9 million in the same period a year ago.
Imports from outside Central America grew 5.1 percent, to $1.174 billion from $1.118 billion.
